title: The Sealed Tomb of the Tide-King
hook: The adventurers' guild of Brackenford pays six hundred gold to whoever opens the sealed tomb beyond the ruined causeway.
truth: The tomb's door answers only to the word for the tide. Its builder hid the three parts of the answer along the old road: a verse at the roadside shrine, a token the hill village keeps, and the marks cut into the causeway's last milestone. Behind the door an old gate stands open onto a far coast.
motive: The tide-king's keeper sealed the gate so only those who walked the old road and read its signs could pass.

scenes.place: A roadside shrine under an old yew, a bronze bell in a stone niche, offerings of salt and shells on its ledge.
dressing: a bronze bell in a stone niche
salt and shells on the ledge
an old yew over the shrine
scenes.danger: Nothing threatens; the road is quiet and the wind moves the yew.
scenes.music: a slow solo fiddle over a low drone, unhurried

scenes.place: A hill village of stone cottages and turf roofs above the river, its elder's house hung with drying nets.
dressing: drying nets on a cottage wall
scenes.danger: Nothing threatens; the villagers are wary of strangers.
scenes.music: a plucked lute and a soft hand drum, homely

scenes.place: A ruined causeway of tilted stones across a tidal marsh, a lichened milestone at its far end.
dressing: reeds and black water on both sides
scenes.danger: The stones shift underfoot and the water between them is deep.
scenes.music: low strings and a hollow wind instrument, uneasy

scenes.place: A tomb cut into a sea cliff, its round stone door carved with waves and a pale disc, an iron grate before it.
dressing: a round stone door carved with waves
a pale stone disc above the door
scenes.danger: The cliff path is narrow and the grate is locked.
scenes.music: a deep sustained choir hum and slow drums, solemn

characters.name: The Tide-King's Keeper
characters.role: The long-dead keeper of the tide-king's tomb, who hid the answer along the road.

guidance.beat: The keeper is long gone; only the signs remain.

evidence.what: A verse cut around the rim of the shrine's bronze bell, in an old script.
evidence.flaw: The verse speaks of a water that climbs the stones and is pulled by the pale lamp of the night.
evidence.up_close: Worn letters in an old script run around the bell's rim, between engraved waves and a small full moon.

evidence.what: A carved bone token the village elder keeps, passed down from the tomb's builders.
evidence.flaw: The token shows the moon above two waves, one high and one low: the water rises and falls as the moon turns.
evidence.up_close: A palm-sized bone disc, carved on one face with a moon over two waves of different heights, polished by many hands.

evidence.what: Marks cut into the last milestone of the causeway.
evidence.flaw: The marks count two comings and two goings in a single day, the way the sea comes up the marsh and draws back.
evidence.up_close: Under the lichen, two arrows point toward the sea and two away from it, set around a single sun.

beats.happens: The party stops at the shrine and finds the bell's verse.
beats.turns_on: Reading the old script on the bell.

beats.happens: The village elder shows the party the bone token.
Across the causeway the party finds the carved milestone.
beats.turns_on: Crossing the broken stones and clearing the lichen.

beats.happens: The sealed door asks its riddle.
beats.turns_on: Putting the three signs together into one answer.

stages.worth_a_look: Herons standing still in the shallows.

stages.sight: The first tilted stones of an old causeway running out over black water.
A narrow path along a sea cliff, gulls wheeling below.
stages.worth_a_look: Old steps cut into the rock, worn hollow.

stages.sight: A ledge before a dark opening in the cliff face.
